subject: Critical Thinking
title: Socrates: The Man Who Knew He Knew Nothing
description: A fast breakdown of Socrates: The Man Who Knew He Knew Nothing for builders.

hook.text: Socrates never wrote a word. He wandered Athens asking questions.

buildup.text: The Oracle at Delphi said no one was wiser than Socrates.

discovery.text: Socrates asked relentless questions until people saw the contradictions hiding inside certainty.

twist.text: Athens executed him for 'corrupting the youth.' His crime: teaching young people to question authority & think for.

climax.text: His legacy: the Socratic method is used in law schools, therapy, & education worldwide.

punchline.text: He knew nothing – & that made him wiser than everyone who thought they knew.

quiz.question: What was Socrates' primary method of philosophical inquiry?

details.summary: Socrates pioneered the method of relentless questioning to expose ignorance and pursue truth. His claim that wisdom begins with recognizing how little you know became the foundation of Western critical thinking.
details.whyItMatters: Socratic questioning remains the most powerful tool for uncovering assumptions and testing beliefs, used in law, therapy, and education to this day.
takeaways: The Socratic method exposes contradictions through dialogue
He was executed for challenging Athenian certainties

faq.question: What is the Socratic method and how does it work in practice?
faq.answer: The Socratic method uses a series of probing questions to guide someone toward discovering contradictions in their own beliefs. Instead of telling people they are wrong, Socrates let their own logic reveal the flaws.

faq.question: Why was Socrates sentenced to death if he was seeking truth?
faq.answer: Socrates exposed the ignorance of powerful Athenians in public, humiliating them. His questioning was seen as corrupting youth and undermining social order, which threatened those in authority.
